name: Jean George
current_role: General Partner, Lightstone Ventures (also GP at Advanced Technology Ventures); Shoulder Innovations insider via Lightstone fund holdings
profile: Boston-based life-science venture capitalist and Forbes Midas List investor. After ~10 years at Genzyme (VP global sales & marketing, founder of its tissue repair division) and leading life-science deals at BancBoston Ventures, she joined ATV in 2002 and co-founded Lightstone Ventures, which co-led financings of Shoulder Innovations (NYSE: SI).
interesting_fact: Led investments in Proteolix (acquired by Onyx), Hypnion (acquired by Eli Lilly) and Acceleron Pharma (IPO 2013, later acquired by Merck); she has appeared on the Forbes Midas List.
deep_cut_fact: A 1980 University of Maine biology graduate who began in bioresearch; she said she chose biotech in the 1980s because 'there were no road maps and you were able to create your own vision for the future.'
notes: Insider filing at Shoulder Innovations is as a fund-affiliated holder ('Other'), not an operator. Best route is via Lightstone Ventures' website contact form.

name: John Caplan
current_role: CEO and Director, Payoneer Global Inc. (Nasdaq: PAYO)
profile: Serial internet/commerce executive who founded e-commerce platform OpenSky (2009), sold it to Alibaba in 2017 and then ran Alibaba.com for North America & Europe until 2021. He joined Payoneer as co-CEO in 2022 and became sole CEO in 2023, leading the cross-border payments platform for SMBs and freelancers worldwide.
interesting_fact: Before OpenSky he was CMO of About.com and later CEO of Ford Models; at Alibaba he turned OpenSky into Alibaba.com's North America B2B business.
deep_cut_fact: His family founded fine-jeweler Oscar Heyman & Brothers in New York in 1912 after emigrating from Latvia; he and his cousins still sit on its board.
notes: Frequent podcast/conference guest (e.g. Fintech Blueprint, NYSE IPO Edge) - receptive to media. Go via Payoneer PR.

name: Ryals McMullian
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Flowers Foods, Inc. (NYSE: FLO)
profile: A. Ryals McMullian Jr. joined Thomasville, Georgia-based Flowers Foods in 2003 as associate general counsel and rose through M&A, deputy GC, chief strategy officer and COO roles to become CEO in 2019 and chairman in 2023. He runs one of the largest US packaged-bread makers (Nature's Own, Dave's Killer Bread, Wonder, Tastykake), and has pushed into adjacencies via deals such as Canyon Bakehouse and Simple Mills.
interesting_fact: A lawyer by training rather than a baker: he holds a BS in finance and real estate, an MBA and a JD, all from Florida State University, and is a member of the Georgia Bar.
deep_cut_fact: Before the top job he ran Flowers' M&A as VP and deputy general counsel; he also serves as a trustee of Florida TaxWatch, on the Consumer Brands Association board, and on the Georgia Research Alliance board.
notes: Low public profile outside trade press (Baking Business, Shelby Report). Media route is Flowers' contact page.

name: Mark Alan Peterson
current_role: EVP, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, EPR Properties (NYSE: EPR)
profile: Kansas City-based CPA who has been CFO and Treasurer of experiential real-estate REIT EPR Properties (theatres, ski resorts, attractions, eat-and-play venues) since 2006, after joining as VP in 2004; promoted to EVP in 2015. He oversees accounting, capital planning, treasury and IT. Previously VP accounting & finance at American Italian Pasta Co.
interesting_fact: EPR's portfolio is built around 'experiential' properties - movie theatres, ski areas, water parks and attractions - and he has run its capital markets activity for nearly two decades.
deep_cut_fact: From 1995 to 1998 he was CFO of the J.C. Nichols Company - the Kansas City developer behind the Country Club Plaza - until its acquisition by Highwoods Properties; he earned a B.S. in Accounting with highest honors from the University of Illinois (1986).
notes: Corporate finance executive with minimal public profile; not a founder. Route via EPR investor relations.

name: Mary G Meeker
current_role: Founder and General Partner, BOND (Bond Capital), San Francisco; director of Block, Inc.
profile: Former Morgan Stanley internet analyst dubbed the 'Queen of the Internet' for her annual Internet Trends reports (since 1995). She moved to Kleiner Perkins in 2010 and in 2018 founded growth fund BOND, raising $1.25B for fund I and $2B for fund II, with early bets such as Canva. In May 2025 she returned with BOND's first 'Trends - Artificial Intelligence' report.
interesting_fact: Her Internet Trends deck became one of tech's most-read annual documents; she championed Netscape, AOL, Amazon, eBay and Google early, and in 2025 published a 340-page AI trends report framing AI as a US-China 'space race'.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Portland, Indiana, she was captain of the golf team at Jay County High School thanks to her 'golf nut' father; she started on Wall Street as a Merrill Lynch stockbroker in 1982 after a psychology degree from DePauw.
notes: Very press-averse; rarely gives interviews, speaks mainly through her Trends reports. AI/data-center themes of her 2025 report fit the podcast. No published direct email found; route via BOND.

name: Emily White
current_role: President, Anthos Capital (consumer-focused PE/VC); director of lululemon athletica and Olaplex
profile: Silicon Valley operator who spent nine years at Google, then ran business operations at Facebook and Instagram before serving as Snapchat's COO (2013-2015), where she launched the company's first ad product. She later founded concierge startup Mave and now invests via Anthos Capital while sitting on consumer-brand boards.
interesting_fact: As Snapchat COO she oversaw the 2014 rollout of its first revenue stream, 'Brand Story' ads, and the Samsung-sponsored American Music Awards story stream.
deep_cut_fact: A Castilleja School and Vanderbilt (2000) alumna from Santa Clara, she was a board observer at Hyperloop One from 2015 and founded an invite-only personal-concierge startup, Mave, in 2016.
notes: Current Anthos title is per Wikipedia; could not re-verify on the firm's sparse site. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so research relied on Wikipedia and company sites.

name: Dennis Woodside
current_role: CEO and President, Freshworks Inc. (Nasdaq: FRSH)
profile: Lawyer-turned-tech operator: Second Circuit clerk, Munger Tolles and McKinsey, then Google (EMEA sales ops, SVP Americas), CEO of Motorola Mobility (2012-14), Dropbox COO (2014-18) and president of Impossible Foods (2019-22). He joined Freshworks as president in 2022 and became CEO in 2024; the AI-driven service-software company passed $1B ARR in late 2026.
interesting_fact: He ran Motorola Mobility for Google from 2012 until its sale to Lenovo, then helped scale Dropbox through its 2018 IPO, then took a detour into plant-based meat at Impossible Foods.
deep_cut_fact: A 15-time Ironman finisher with a 9:22 personal best at Ironman Arizona 2016, where he placed 2nd in his age group and qualified for the 2017 Kona World Championship; he also rowed at Cornell, earning two varsity letters.
notes: Media-friendly public-company CEO; route via Freshworks PR.

name: Charles Crocker
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Crocker Capital (private investment company), San Francisco; retired from Teledyne board April 2025
profile: San Francisco technology industrialist (born c.1938/39) who led sensor and electronics maker BEI Electronics / BEI Technologies as chairman and CEO from 1995 until its 2005 sale to Schneider Electric, then ran Schneider's Custom Sensors & Technologies division to 2006. He served on Teledyne's board 2001-2025 and on Franklin Resources' board 2003-2014; he now invests through Crocker Capital.
interesting_fact: Sat on Teledyne Technologies' board for 24 years (2001-2025), with the board formally thanking him for his 'sage advice' on his retirement.
deep_cut_fact: A major San Francisco civic figure: he has chaired the board of Children's Hospital in San Francisco, chaired the Hamlin School's trustees and served as president of the Foundation of the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco.
notes: Aged ~87; retired from Teledyne board Apr 2025 (2026 proxy gives no indication of death, but status not independently confirmed). No published contact found; Crocker Capital has no public website located. Bio from Teledyne 2024 proxy (DEF 14A filed 2024-03-15).

name: Jeffrey Kaditz
current_role: Unknown (2026); Affirm co-founder, widely reported as founder of whole-body-scan health company Q Bio, whose 2026 leadership page no longer lists him
profile: Software entrepreneur who co-founded buy-now-pay-later lender Affirm in 2012 with Max Levchin, Nathan Gettings and Alex Rampell. He subsequently founded Q Bio (2015, Redwood City), a 'quantitative biology' preventive-health company built around a whole-body MRI 'Q Exam'; Q Bio is now run by CEO Jeffrey Brewer.
interesting_fact: One of four Affirm co-founders alongside PayPal co-founder Max Levchin; Affirm went on to partner with Apple Pay in 2024.

name: Sam Lown
current_role: Founder & CTO, Invopop (global e-invoicing infrastructure, Madrid)
profile: Madrid-based software engineer who joined Cabify as CTO in July 2011, its founding year, helping build Spain's first unicorn ride-hailing company. He later founded Invopop, an API platform that converts invoices into the legally required e-invoice formats in 30+ countries and sends them to tax authorities. Cabify co-founders Vicente Pascual and Adrian Merino back it.
interesting_fact: Joined Cabify as CTO two months after Juan de Antonio founded it in May 2011; Cabify became Spain's first unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Invopop is built on GOBL, an open-source 'global invoicing in JSON' standard and global tax-rules database that converts one JSON invoice into local formats such as CFDI, UBL, FacturaE and FatturaPA; investors include former Oracle CFO Jeff Epstein.
notes: Source lists him as Cabify 'founder'; Wikipedia describes him as early CTO (joined July 2011). Active builder/engineer - likely receptive to a tech podcast.

name: David Gurle
current_role: CEO, Antimatter (2026 merger of Hivenet, PoliCloud and Data Factory - modular, energy-located AI data centers and distributed cloud)
profile: French engineer and IP-communications pioneer who ran Microsoft's Real Time Communications unit (NetMeeting, Windows Messenger), Reuters Messaging and Skype's business unit, then founded encrypted-messaging startup Perzo, which became Symphony, the Wall Street messaging platform he led as CEO from 2014. Since 2022 he has built Hivenet and PoliCloud, now merged into Antimatter.
interesting_fact: Antimatter builds modular micro-data centers 'deployed where energy already exists' and in 2026 signed a EUR580M framework deal with CloudGrid Energy for 280 PoliCloud units - squarely on the podcast's energy/data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: Raised between Turkey, Syria and Lebanon, his family settled in Cannes when he was 14 - and in Feb 2025 Cannes became the first European city to deploy his PoliCloud sovereign, decentralized cloud. He also co-wrote books on IP telephony/VoIP.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy/data-center podcast; actively doing press (Hivenet/Antimatter press page, named Top AI Entrepreneur at European AI Awards). Legion d'honneur 2020 (Wikipedia, citation needed).

name: David Barrett
profile: One of four Irish co-founders of customer-messaging/AI-support company Intercom (now Fin), founded in California in 2011 with Eoghan McCabe, Des Traynor and Ciaran Lee; the four had earlier built bug-tracking tool Exceptional at their design consultancy Contrast and sold it to Rackspace in 2011 to fund Intercom.
interesting_fact: Intercom was seeded with the proceeds of selling the founders' earlier product, Exceptional, to Rackspace in 2011.
notes: Do not confuse with David Barrett, founder/CEO of Expensify. The Intercom co-founder keeps a very low profile; current role not found. Web search budget exhausted, so only Wikipedia/Irish Times checked.

name: Rick Klausner
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Scientist and Board Co-Chair, Altos Labs (cellular rejuvenation); co-founder of Lyell Immunopharma
profile: Richard D. Klausner, MD, was the 11th director of the US National Cancer Institute (1995-2001) and executive director of global health at the Gates Foundation (2002-05). He became a prolific biotech founder - Juno Therapeutics (2013), GRAIL (2015), Lyell Immunopharma (2018, CAR-T cell therapy) and Altos Labs (2022), where he is chief scientist - and was Illumina's CMO 2013-16.
interesting_fact: He co-founded GRAIL, the multi-cancer early-detection blood-test company, and Juno Therapeutics (acquired by Celgene), before helping launch the ~$3B-funded longevity company Altos Labs.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Yale studying physics, then switched to biology intending to become a doctor in a rural area; as a child he used to visit his chemist father's laboratory. At 30 he became chief of the NICHD's cell biology and metabolism branch.
notes: Elected to the National Academy of Sciences (1993); 300+ scientific papers. Best route via Altos Labs media.

name: Sofia Nunes
profile: Co-founder of Mambu, the Berlin-born, Amsterdam-headquartered cloud core-banking SaaS company valued at $5.3B in Dec 2021. Mambu grew out of a Carnegie Mellon Master of Human-Computer Interaction capstone project in which she was the team's psychology specialist; she and two teammates turned the thesis into a platform for microfinance institutions in Latin America and Africa.
interesting_fact: Mambu's origins lie in student field research on microfinance institutions in Mozambique; it now powers banks and fintechs worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: On the five-person Carnegie Mellon HCI capstone team that conceived Mambu, her role was 'psychology' - alongside Eugene Danilkis (project management) and Frederik Pfisterer (technology).
notes: Very low public profile; current role unknown and she may no longer be involved operationally. Web search budget exhausted, so personal channels not found.

name: Gregory Maxwell
current_role: Independent Bitcoin developer/cryptographer (former co-founder and CTO of Blockstream; left the company in 2017)
profile: Longtime Bitcoin Core contributor and cryptographer who co-founded Bitcoin infrastructure company Blockstream in 2014 with Adam Back, Pieter Wuille and others. He is known for privacy and scaling proposals in Bitcoin (e.g. CoinJoin, Confidential Transactions) and has worked largely independently since leaving Blockstream.
interesting_fact: Blockstream, which he co-founded, builds Bitcoin sidechains (Liquid), Lightning tooling and privacy enhancements, and is headquartered in Menlo Park with offices in Lugano and Tokyo.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bitcoin he worked on open audio codecs at the Xiph.Org Foundation: he ran and published the 2011 64 kbit/s multiformat listening test that Wikipedia cites as evidence for the Opus codec's quality versus AAC, Vorbis and MP3.
notes: Highly technical and famously media-averse; communicates mostly on technical forums (e.g. as 'nullc' on Reddit/Bitcoin dev lists). No published contact found. CoinJoin/CT attribution and 2017 Blockstream exit are from general knowledge - verify.

name: Richmond Teo
current_role: Co-founder, Paxos (formerly CEO of Paxos Asia; no longer on Paxos' 2026 leadership page - current role not found)
profile: Co-founded Paxos with Charles Cascarilla in 2012 as the itBit bitcoin exchange; in 2015 it became Paxos Trust Company, one of the first NYDFS-chartered crypto trust companies, and grew into a major stablecoin issuer and blockchain-infrastructure provider (now a national bank). Teo led the company's Asia business from Singapore.
interesting_fact: Paxos began life in 2012 as itBit, a bitcoin exchange, before pivoting into regulated stablecoin issuance and tokenization infrastructure.
notes: Not listed on Paxos's current leadership page (https://www.paxos.com/leadership); Paxos publishes no press email (only a contact page). Web search budget exhausted - revisit for his current venture.

name: Amber Venz Box
profile: A content creator turned founder, she started rewardStyle in 2011 with Baxter Box (now LTK's CEO) to let bloggers and lifestyle creators earn commissions on the products they recommend - a model LTK calls 'Creator Commerce'. LTK now drives $6B+ in annual consumer sales across 8,000 retailers, 1M brands and 160+ countries.
interesting_fact: LTK says its platform has produced nearly 1,100 'LTK millionaires' among creators and brands, and has paid out $3B+ to creators.
deep_cut_fact: She has hosted her own LTK video series, 'Talk Shop with Amber Venz Box', with a candid segment called 'Candidly Amber', and interviewed Olympic gymnast Nastia Liukin about life after competition and building a brand on LTK.

public_contacts.value: 'More to Say' (LTK podcast, linked from company site)

notes: Very media-friendly; frequent podcast and TV guest. Best route: LTK press email.
